Replace every `Err(PgError::unimplemented("EXE-42", ...))` body of the file with a real implementation; do not change any signature, pub item, `// CONTRACT` item, other file, Cargo.toml or dependency; no todo!/unimplemented!/panic!/unwrap/expect on user-derived data (use PgError constructors from `crate::error` for executor errors and the lower layers' constructors for theirs). You CANNOT compile or run anything: write simple, explicit Rust, re-read every function once for borrow/ownership/type errors, and use only APIs whose definitions you have READ in the files under `reads` or in the dependency sources (~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/, PostgreSQL reference in ~/develop/reference/postgres-18: cite paths in comments, never copy code). Remove `#[allow(unused_variables)]` from functions you implement. Add unit tests in a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the bottom of the file using `crate::memtxn::MemTxn` as the transaction and `pgarbor_catalog::testing` for catalogs; tests that need other not-yet-implemented leases are marked `#[ignore = "needs <LEASE>"]`. Implement per module docs with `pgarbor_catalog::acl::{RoleGraph::build(snapshot, database), effective_acl, privilege_mask, AclObject}` and `model::acl_mode`. Superuser/owner semantics are inside `privilege_mask`. Errors via `pgarbor_catalog::errors::permission_denied_for`. Unit tests with a catalog containing two roles and GRANT/REVOKE applied through `CatalogTxn::grant_object_privileges`.
acceptance: a role without privileges gets 42501 `permission denied for table t` on SELECT/INSERT; after GRANT SELECT the SELECT passes and INSERT still fails
column-level GRANT SELECT (a) lets `select a` pass and `select b` fail
the owner and superusers always pass
pg_catalog relations are readable by everyone
